questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given a, b, c are in G.P.

Let common ratio of G.P. be r , then b=ar, c=ar2

Given equation can be written as

a+ar+ar2=x. a. r

⇒x=r+1r+1

As we know r>0, then r+1r≥2⇒x≥3

r<0, then r+1r≤-2⇒x≤-1

⇒x∈-∞,-1∪3, ∞

Hence, x ≠2.

questions.q: Let $a_1, a_2, a_3 \ldots$ be in an A.P. such that $\sum_{\mathrm{k}=1}^{12} \mathrm{a}_{2 \mathrm{k}-1}=-\frac{72}{5} \mathrm{a}_1, \mathrm{a}_1 \neq 0$. If $\sum_{\mathrm{k}=1}^{\mathrm{n}} \mathrm{a}_{\mathrm{k}}=0$, then n is:
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Let $a_1=a$, common difference $=d$
$a_1+a_3+a_5+\ldots \ldots+a_{23}=-\frac{72}{5} a$
$\frac{12}{2}[2 a+11 \times 2 d]=-\frac{72}{5} a$
$12 a+132 d=-\frac{72}{5} a$
$132 a+132 \times 5 d=0$
$\mathrm{a}=-5 \mathrm{~d}$
$\frac{\mathrm{n}}{2}(2 \mathrm{a}+(\mathrm{n}-1) \mathrm{d})=0 \Rightarrow-10 \mathrm{~d}+\mathrm{nd}-\mathrm{d}=0$
$\mathrm{n}=11$

questions.q: Suppose that the number of terms in an A.P. is $2 k, k \in N$. If the sum of all odd terms of the A.P. is 40 , the sum of all even terms is 55 and the last term of the A.P. exceeds the first term by 27, then k is equal to :
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Let the A.P. be
$\begin{aligned}
& a, a+2, a+2 d, \ldots, a+(2 k-1) d \\
& \text { Now, } a+a+2 d+a+4 d+\ldots+a+(2 k-2) d=40 \\
& k a+2 d+4 d+\ldots+(2 k-2) d=40 \\
& \Rightarrow k a+\frac{k-1}{2}[2 d+2 k d-2 d]=40
\end{aligned}\Rightarrow k a+k(k-1) d=40$  ...(1)
And $a+d+a+3 d+\ldots+a+(2 k-1) d=55\Rightarrow k a+\frac{k}{2}(d+2 k d-d)=55\Rightarrow k a+k^2 d=55$  ....(2)
Also, $a+(2 k-1) d-a=27\Rightarrow \quad(2 k-1) d=27 \Rightarrow d=\frac{27}{2 k-1}$  ...(3)
From equation (1) and (2)
$k^2 d-k d-k^2 d=-15\Rightarrow \quad d=\frac{15}{k}$
From equation (3) and (4)
$\begin{aligned}
& \frac{27}{2 k-1}=\frac{15}{k} \\
& 27 k=30 k-15 \\
& \Rightarrow 3 k=15 \\
& \Rightarrow k=5
\end{aligned}$

questions.q: Three numbers are in an increasing geometric progression with common ratio <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>r</mi><mo>.</mo></math> If the middle number is doubled, then the new numbers are in an arithmetic progression with common difference <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>d</mi><mo>.</mo></math> If the fourth term of GP is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>,</mo></math> then <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>-</mo><mi>d</mi></math> is equal to :

questions.solution:
Three numbers are in an increasing geometric progression with common ratio r.

Let first term is a

⇒ar,a,ar ∈ G.P 

Given that if middle term is doubled 

 ⇒ar,2a,ar ∈ A.P 

If a, b, c ∈ A. P ⇒ 2b =a + c
4a=ar+ar

4=r+1r

r2+1=4r

r2-4r+1=0 

Ifax2 + bx +c = 0 ⇒ x = -b ± b2-4ac2ac

⇒r=4±122=2+3,2-3

But it is an increasing G. P

∴ r = 2 + 3

Given that Fourth term of G.P ⇒ t4 = ar2 = 3r2

⇒ a = 3.

Common difference of an A.P = d = t2 - t1

d=2a-ar=a2-1r=32-12+3

=3(2-2+3)=33
Hence r2-d=(2+3)2-(33)

= 4 + 3 + 43 - 33

=7+3

questions.q: The sum of an infinite geometric series with positive terms is 3 and the sum of the cubes of its terms is $\frac{27}{19}$. Then the common ratio of this series is:
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Let the terms of infinite series are $a, a r, a r^{2}, a r^{3}, \ldots$

So, $\quad \frac{a}{1-r}=3$

Since, sum of cubes of its terms is $\frac{27}{19}$ that is sum of $a^{3}$,

$a^{3} r^{3}, \ldots \infty$ is $\frac{27}{19}$

So, $\frac{a^{3}}{1-r^{3}}=\frac{27}{19}\Rightarrow \quad \frac{a}{1-r} \times \frac{a^{2}}{\left(1+r^{2}+r\right)}=\frac{27}{19}\Rightarrow \frac{9\left(1+r^{2}-2 r\right) \times 3}{1+r^{2}+r}=\frac{27}{19}\Rightarrow \quad 6 r^{2}-13 r+6=0\Rightarrow(3 r-2)(2 r-3)=0\Rightarrow r=\frac{2}{3},$ or $\frac{3}{2}$

As $|r|  \lt  1$

So, $r=\frac{2}{3}$

questions.q:
Let $x, y$ be positive real numbers and $m, n$ positive integers.

The maximum value of the expression $\frac{x^{\mathrm{m}} y^{\mathrm{n}}}{\left(1+x^{2 \mathrm{~m}}\right)\left(1+y^{2 \mathrm{n}}\right)}$

is :
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$A=\frac{x^{m} y^{n}}{\left(1+x^{2 m}\right)\left(1+y^{2 n}\right)}=\frac{1}{\left(x^{-m}+x^{m}\right)\left(y^{-n}+y^{n}\right)}\frac{x^{m}+y^{-m}}{2} \geq\left(x^{n+1}, x^{-m}\right)^{\frac{1}{2}} \Rightarrow x^{n+}+x^{-n} \geq 2$

In the same way, $y^{n}+y^{n} \geq 2$

Then $,\left(x^{n}+x^{-n}\right)\left(y^{-n}+y^{n}\right) \geq 4\Rightarrow \frac{1}{\left(x^{\text {"1 }}+x^{-m}\right)\left(y^{-n}+y^{n}\right)} \leq \frac{1}{4}$

questions.q: Let <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>n</mi></msub></math> be the sum of the first <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>n</mi></math> terms of an arithmetic progression. If <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>i</mi><mfenced><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>-</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></mfenced><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>≤</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>≤</mo><mn>100</mn></math>, then the mean of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>y</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo></math>, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>y</mi><mn>100</mn></msub></math> is
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

Mean of x1, x2..........,x100 is 200

So, the sum of observation will be,

∑xi=100×200

Now using the sum of A.P formula in above equation as all terms are in arithmetic progression we get,

1002x1+x100=100×200

⇒502+x100=100×200

⇒x100=398

⇒x1+99d=398

⇒d=4

Now, xi=2+(i-1)4=4i-2

So, yi=ixi-i=3i2-2i

Now finding mean we get,

y¯=1100∑yi

⇒y¯=1100∑3i2-2i

⇒y¯=11003×100×101×2016-2100×1012

⇒y¯=101×2012-101

⇒y¯=10049.5

questions.q: The number of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn></math>-digit numbers, that are divisible by either <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn></math> or <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn></math> but not divisible by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>7</mn></math> is _____ .
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
We know that total number of three-digit number will be 900,

Now let nA be number of three-digit number which are divisible by 2, i.e,

A=100,102,...,998

⇒nA=450

nB be number of three-digit number which are divisible by 3, i.e, B=102,105,...,999

nB=300

Numbers divisible by both 2 and 3 is

102,108,...996 i.e, 150

Numbers divisible by both 2 and 7 are 112,126,...,994 i.e., 64 numbers.

Numbers divisible by both 3 and 7 is 105,126,...987 i.e, 43 numbers.

Numbers divisible by 2,3 & 7 is 126,168,...,966 i.e, 21 numbers.

Required number

=450+150-64-43+21=514

Hence, 514 three-digit number are there which are divisible by 2 or 3 but not divisible by 7.

=0.16log2.5131-13=425log5212

=52-2log5212=12-2=4

questions.q: Consider an arithmetic series and a geometric series having four initial terms from the set <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced open="{" close="}"><mrow><mn>11</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>21</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>16</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>26</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>32</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></mfenced></math>. If the last terms of these series are the maximum possible four digit numbers, then the number of common terms in these two series is equal to _______.
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given set=11,8,21,16,26,32,4

Given an arithmetic series and a geometric series having the first four terms from the given set. 

Then, 

Geometric series : 4,8,16,32,64,128,256,512,1024,2048,4096,8192

Arithmetic series: 11,16,21,26,31,36,...,256,....4096,...

Tn (G.P.)=4·2n-1

Tn (A.P.)=11+5n-1=5n+6

For common terms, 4·2n-1=5n+6

So, common terms are 16,256,4096 only.

questions.q: If <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> arithmetic means (A.Ms) and three geometric means (G.Ms) are inserted between <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>243</mn></math> such that <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mn>4</mn><mrow><mi>t</mi><mi>h</mi></mrow></msup></math> A.M. is equal to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mn>2</mn><mrow><mi>n</mi><mi>d</mi></mrow></msup></math> G.M., then <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>m</mi></math> is equal to:
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Let 3, A1, A2, A3,......Am, 243 are in arithmetic progression with m arithmetic means.

Common difference d=243-3m+1=240m+1

Let 3, G1, G2, G3, 243 are in geometric progression with 3 geometric means.

Common ratio r=243313+1=8114=3

Given G2=A4

⇒332=3+4240m+1

⇒27=3+960m+1

⇒m+1=40

⇒m=39

questions.q: If three successive terms of a G.P. with common ratio <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>r</mi><mfenced><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>></mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfenced></math> are the length of the sides of a triangle and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced close="]" open="["><mi>r</mi></mfenced></math> denotes the greatest integer less than or equal to r, then <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn><mfenced close="]" open="["><mi>r</mi></mfenced><mo>+</mo><mfenced close="]" open="["><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow></mfenced></math> is equal to:
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Let, a,ar,ar2→G.P.

It is given that sum of any two sides is greater than the third side.

⇒a+ar>ar2, a+ar2>ar, ar+ar2>a

Case-I: r2−r−1<0

⇒r=1±1-4×1×-12

⇒r=1±52

⇒r∈1−52,1+52   ...i

Case-II: r2−r+1>0 is always true.

Case-III: r2+r−1>0

⇒r∈−∞,−1−52∪−1+52,∞   ...ii

Taking intersection of i and ii

⇒r∈−1+52,1+52

As r>1

⇒r∈1,1+52

⇒r=1 and −r=−2

⇒3r+−r=3-2

⇒3r+−r=1
